item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: add some music to this clip

dialog.agent:
I can create a music track, but the connected tools can’t mix it into your existing clip.

What mood would you like—**upbeat, cinematic, or chill**—and how long is the clip? I can make a matching track for you to add in a video editor.
dialog.why: It asks the user to choose a mood and provide the clip length, then waits before creating a matching music track.

dialog.agent:
Tense instrumental, no vocals—got it. The music generator has a **15-second minimum**, and I can’t mix or trim it into your clip with the connected tools.

Would you like a 15-second track designed so you can use its first 7 seconds? It costs **15 Magic Hour credits**.
dialog.why: It asks the user to approve generating a 15-second track for 15 credits and waits for confirmation.

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the generation because your account has **insufficient credits**. No track was created.

The 15-second instrumental needs **15 credits**. Once those are available, I can try again.

approvals.name: generate_music

style.prompt: Tense cinematic instrumental underscore for a seven-second video clip, delivered as a fifteen-second track. No singing, no vocals, no spoken words, no choir. Begin immediately with a low ominous synth drone, a restrained ticking pulse and dark, subtle percussive accents. Build suspense quickly within the first five seconds, with a controlled cinematic impact at six seconds and a short decay ending cleanly by seven seconds, so the first seven seconds can be used as a self-contained cue. After that, maintain a quiet atmospheric instrumental tail through fifteen seconds. Minimal, suspenseful, polished, no upbeat melodies.
